16.text: Good intentions don't guarantee good outcomes.

17.text: Most ethical questions are about weighing competing goods.

19.text: Honesty is easier in a kind environment.

20.text: Cruelty often hides behind small habits.

25.text: Hypocrisy is easier to see in others.

29.text: Power tests character more than poverty does.

30.text: Doing nothing is also a choice.

34.text: Courage is acting well while afraid.

35.text: We can be confident and wrong at the same time.

36.text: Evidence is what changes a careful mind.

37.text: Most beliefs come in groups, not one at a time.

38.text: We tend to remember the times we were right.

42.text: Models are wrong but some are useful.

47.text: The smartest people change their minds the most.

48.text: Disagreement is not the same as misunderstanding.

49.text: Sometimes both sides are partly right.

50.text: The world is older than any explanation of it.

51.text: Consciousness is the strangest thing we know.

52.text: We see less of the world than we think.

55.text: The mind builds the world it lives in.

64.text: The present is the only place anything ever happens.

65.text: Socrates said the unexamined life is not worth living.

66.text: The Stoics tried to want only what they had.

67.text: Confucius taught the importance of small rituals.

68.text: The Buddha pointed to the cause of suffering.

69.text: Aristotle thought virtue was a habit, not a feeling.

70.text: Plato suspected the things we see are like shadows.

71.text: Lao Tzu praised the way of water.

72.text: Epicurus wanted peaceful pleasures, not grand ones.

74.text: Many traditions agree more than they disagree.

75.text: Kant said treat people as ends, not just means.

76.text: Hume noticed that reason alone doesn't make us care.

77.text: Nietzsche wrote that hard truths can also be gifts.

78.text: Wittgenstein said the limits of our language are the limits of our world.

79.text: Simone de Beauvoir argued that we become ourselves through our choices.

80.text: William James said belief shapes what we can do.

81.text: John Rawls asked what rules we'd accept if we didn't know who we'd be.

82.text: Hannah Arendt warned that evil can be ordinary.

83.text: Iris Murdoch said love is the hard work of paying attention.

84.text: Many modern philosophers borrow freely from many traditions.

85.text: Begin with the work you can actually do today.

86.text: Listen as if you might be wrong.

87.text: Try to want less before earning more.

88.text: Notice what you do when no one is watching.

89.text: A walk is a small philosophy.

90.text: The hardest argument to make is the one you owe yourself.

91.text: Hold opinions the way you hold a tool.

92.text: Take other people's words at their best.

93.text: Practice gratitude on ordinary mornings, not just special ones.

94.text: The shortest road is sometimes through the question.

95.text: Wonder is a kind of attention.

96.text: Read old books at least sometimes.

97.text: Disagree well and the relationship survives.

98.text: A good life is many small good days.
